Slide.Title: labor (noun)
Slide.SlideText: labor (noun) Definition: Definition: work or workers Synonyms: Synonyms: work, effort, undertaking Examples: Examples: Industrial countries require a lot of skilled labor. Carpentry and bricklaying are examples of manual labor. Plumbers are well paid for their labor. Plumbers are well paid for their labor.

Slide.Title: lack (verb)
Slide.SlideText: lack (verb) Definition: Definition: to be without Synonyms: Synonyms: miss, need, require Examples: Examples: She lacks motivation to finish the job. The kitchen lacks a dishwasher. The puzzle is incomplete; it lacks five pieces. The puzzle is incomplete; it lacks five pieces.

Slide.Title: lake (noun)
Slide.SlideText: lake (noun) Definition: Definition: a large area of fresh water surrounded by land Synonyms: Synonyms: pond, lagoon Examples: Examples: We rented a cabin by a lake. Lake Baikal in Russia, is the deepest lake in the world. The lake is surrounded by mountains. The lake is surrounded by mountains.

Slide.Title: land (verb)
Slide.SlideText: land (verb) Definition: Definition: to come to the earth from the air Synonyms: Synonyms: alight, settle, touchdown Examples: Examples: The bread landed on the floor upside down. A large bird landed on the window sill. The airplane landed safely on the runway. The airplane landed safely on the runway.

Slide.Title: last (verb)
Slide.SlideText: last (verb) Definition: Definition: to continue Synonyms: Synonyms: endure, persist, remain Examples: Examples: Plastic in landfills lasts for hundreds of years. After the fire, the smell of smoke in the air lasted for days. The telephone call lasted six hours. The telephone call lasted six hours.

Slide.Title: lead (verb)
Slide.SlideText: lead (verb) Definition: Definition: to show the way to others, usually by going first Synonyms: Synonyms: guide; direct; head Examples: Examples: The team captain led the players onto the field. The teacher led the class in singing a song. The group hired a guide to lead the hike. The group hired a guide to lead the hike.

Slide.Title: leave (verb)
Slide.SlideText: leave (verb) Definition: Definition: 1) to go away from; 2) to let something stay where it is Synonyms: Synonyms: depart, exit; abandon, renounce Examples: Examples: We don’t know why he had to leave. She will have to leave the building. He left the building at about 6 p.m. He left the building at about 6 p.m.

Slide.Title: legal (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: legal (adjective) Definition: Definition: of or in agreement with the law Synonyms: Synonyms: lawful Examples: Examples: It’s legal for citizens to carry guns in many states. In many places it isn’t legal to walk a dog on the beach. The legal system in America is the world’s finest. The legal system in America is the world’s finest.

Slide.Title: less (adverb)
Slide.SlideText: less (adverb) Definition: Definition: smaller in amount; not as much as Synonyms: Synonyms: fewer Examples: Examples: A Ford car costs less than a Mercedes Benz. Diane eats less than her sister does. The smaller basket holds less than the large one. The smaller basket holds less than the large one.

Slide.Title: let (verb)
Slide.SlideText: let (verb) Definition: Definition: to permit to do or to be; to make possible Synonyms: Synonyms: allow, sanction; cause, enable Examples: Examples: Ming does not let her sister borrow her clothes. My boss would not let me leave work early. Dad, will you please let me borrow the car? Dad, will you please let me borrow the car?

Slide.Title: level (noun)
Slide.SlideText: level (noun) Definition: Definition: the amount of height that something reaches or rises to; the position of something or someone Synonyms: Synonyms: altitude, height, stage Examples: Examples: Before retiring from her company, Anna reached the level of vice president. The flood water reached the level of the windows. I rode the elevator to the third level. I rode the elevator to the third level.

Slide.Title: lie (verb)
Slide.SlideText: lie (verb) Definition: Definition: 1) to have one’s body on the ground or other surface; 2) to say something that one knows is not true Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) recline, repose, sprawl; 2) deceive, falsify, perjure Examples: Examples: He lied about taking the money. (deceive) The dog lay under the desk. (recline) My sister loves to lie in the grass on a sunny day. (recline) My sister loves to lie in the grass on a sunny day.

Slide.Title: life (noun)
Slide.SlideText: life (noun) Definition: Definition: 1) the time between birth and death; 2) all living things Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) existence; 2) animals, creatures Examples: Examples: My grandfather’s life was long and happy. (existence) My dog has a wonderful life. (existence) Coral reefs attract a variety of beautiful marine life. (creatures) Coral reefs attract a variety of beautiful marine life.

Slide.Title: lift (verb)
Slide.SlideText: lift (verb) Definition: Definition: to take or bring up to a higher place or level Synonyms: Synonyms: elevate, hoist, raise Examples: Examples: She has a bad back. It’s hard for her to lift things. We hired a crane to lift the new air conditioner and place it on the roof. Can you help me lift this? Can you help me lift this?

Slide.Title: light (noun)
Slide.SlideText: light (noun) Definition: Definition: 1) a form of energy that affects the eyes so that one is able to see; 2) anything that produces light Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) brightness, illumination; 2) match, lantern, lamp Examples: Examples: Have you got a light? (match) She is sensitive to light, so she wears sunglasses. (brightness) A light bulb gives light. (lamp) A light bulb gives light.

Slide.Title: lightning (noun)
Slide.SlideText: lightning (noun) Definition: Definition: light produced by electricity in the air, usually during a storm Synonyms: Synonyms: bolt Examples: Examples: He has been struck by lightning three times. The lightning lit up the sky. The thunderstorm produced a lot of lightning. The thunderstorm produced a lot of lightning.

Slide.Title: limit (noun)
Slide.SlideText: limit (noun) Definition: Definition: boundary; an amount or degree that cannot be passed Synonyms: Synonyms: bound, end, extent, maximum Examples: Examples: Children need limits in order to feel secure. There is a limit to how much time I can spend working on the computer. It’s dangerous to drive faster than the speed limit. It’s dangerous to drive faster than the speed limit.

Slide.Title: line (noun)
Slide.SlideText: line (noun) Definition: Definition: 1) a long, thin mark on a surface; 2) a number of people or things organized one after another Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) rule, mark; 2) queue, row Examples: Examples: He drew a straight line on the paper. (rule) He stood in line for an hour. The visitors waited in a long line to get into the museum. (queue) The visitors waited in a long line to get into the museum.

Slide.Title: link (verb)
Slide.SlideText: link (verb) Definition: Definition: 1) to connect; 2) to unite one thing or event with another Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) bind, fasten, tie; 2) relate Examples: Examples: The events were closely linked. (relate) My name links me with my ancestors. (relate) A chain is made up of many links. (bind) A chain is made up of many links.

Slide.Title: liquid (noun)
Slide.SlideText: liquid (noun) Definition: Definition: a substance that is not a solid or gas, and can move freely, like water Synonyms: Synonyms: fluid, solution Examples: Examples: The medicine was a brown liquid. When you have a cold, you should drink plenty of liquids. I prefer soap as a liquid rather than a bar. Liquid.

Slide.Title: list (verb)
Slide.SlideText: list (verb) Definition: Definition: to put in writing a number of names of people or things Synonyms: Synonyms: enumerate, tally Examples: Examples: Please list your previous jobs on the application. The nurse told me to list all the medications I was taking. I always list what I need before I go shopping. I always list what I need before I go shopping.

Slide.Title: literature (noun)
Slide.SlideText: literature (noun) Definition: Definition: all the poems, stories, and writings of a period of time or of a country Synonyms: Synonyms: writings, fiction Examples: Examples: She majored in literature at the university. He is a professor of Chinese literature. She likes reading English literature. She likes reading English literature.

Slide.Title: live (verb)
Slide.SlideText: live (verb) Definition: Definition: to have life; to exist Synonyms: Synonyms: subsist, survive, be Examples: Examples: They lived in Spain for several years. His dream is to live in the mountains. Cacti are plants that live in dry places. They live near the beach. They live near the beach.

Slide.Title: loan (noun)
Slide.SlideText: loan (noun) Definition: Definition: money borrowed that usually must be returned with interest payments Synonyms: Synonyms: advance Examples: Examples: He took out a loan in order to buy a car. She asked her family for a loan. A mortgage is a kind of loan that people can use to buy a house. A mortgage is a kind of loan that people can use to buy a house.

Slide.Title: local (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: local (adjective) Definition: Definition: about or having to do with one place Synonyms: Synonyms: civic, regional Examples: Examples: He has breakfast at the local coffee shop every day. This pottery is made by a local artist. Open-air markets sell food grown on local farms. Open-air markets sell food grown on local farms.

Slide.Title: lonely (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: lonely (adjective) Definition: Definition: feeling alone Synonyms: Synonyms: alone, isolated, lonesome, solitary Examples: Examples: Although he has many friends, he is lonely. Working from home via computer can be lonely. Mary was lonely because the other students didn’t talk to her. Mary was lonely because the other students didn’t talk to her.

Slide.Title: lose (verb)
Slide.SlideText: lose (verb) Definition: Definition: to have no longer; be unable to find Synonyms: Synonyms: misplace Examples: Examples: She lost her reading glasses. My dad loses his keys at least once a week. Someone lost a wallet. Someone lost a wallet.

Slide.Title: loud (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: loud (adjective) Definition: Definition: having a strong sound; full of sound or noise Synonyms: Synonyms: blaring, noisy Examples: Examples: Young children can be very loud. The teacher has a loud, clear voice. The loud drill gave her husband a headache. He made sure his message was loud! He made sure his message was loud!

Slide.Title: low (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: low (adjective) Definition: Definition: not high or tall; below the normal height; close to the ground Synonyms: Synonyms: short, shallow Examples: Examples: The chair is too low for me. The books are on a low shelf. You are running low on fuel. You are running low on fuel.

Slide.Title: loyal (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: loyal (adjective) Definition: Definition: showing strong friendship and support for someone or something Synonyms: Synonyms: dependable, faithful, trustworthy Examples: Examples: Mr. Yang’s workers are loyal to him. He is a loyal citizen of his country. She is loyal to her country. She is loyal to her country.
